messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
在 10 kPa（約 0.099 atm）的條件下，水的凝固點大約是 **+0.04 °C**。  
這個值略高於標準大氣壓（101.3 kPa）下的 0 °C，因為水的熔化曲線斜率為負：隨著壓力降低，凝固點會升高。計算可用克勞修斯–克拉佩龍方程估算，得到的差值約為 0.04 °C。
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？" They want the freezing point of water at 10 kPa. We have a tool to calculate boiling point but not freezing point. But we can approximate freezing point shift with Clausius-Clapeyron? However, maybe we can use known data: At 1 atm (101.325 kPa), freezing point is 0°C. At lower pressures, freezing point slightly increases? Actually, freezing point decreases as pressure increases for water? Wait, water has negative slope of melting curve: increasing pressure lowers melting temperature. So at lower pressure (10 kPa < 101 kPa), freezing point should be higher than 0°C. The difference can be estimated using Clapeyron equation: dT/dP = TΔV/ΔH_fusion. For water, ΔV ≈ -9.5e-6 m^3/mol (negative). ΔH_fusion ≈ 6.01e3 J/mol. So dT/dP ≈ T * (-9.5e-6)/6000. At T ~273 K, dT/dP ≈ 273*(-9.5e-6)/6000 ≈ -0.0004325 K/kPa. Negative slope means increasing P lowers T. So decreasing P from 101.3 to 10 kPa (drop of 91.3 kPa) would raise T by about 91.3*0.0004325 ≈ 0.0395 K. So freezing point at 10 kPa ~ +0.04°C. So answer: approx 0.04°C.

We can also mention that at 10 kPa, water freezes at about 0.04°C. Provide explanation. No function call needed.
